## Confidence Interval for a Proportion

You'll work with a dataset called `nuclear_survey` about whether US aduls support nuclear arms reduction. The survey was administered in March 2013. Your goal is to calculate a 95% confidence interval for the proportion of US adults who support arms reduction.

Run the code below to see a random 10 rows of the dataset.
```{code-blanks}
slice_sample(nuclear_survey, n = 10)
```

Answer Questions 9-11 of your packet. Then use those responses to fill in this code to calculate your sample proportion.

```{code-blanks}
#| blank:
#|   target: arms_reduction
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: favor
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: "prop"
#|   prefill: true
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token

sample_prop <- nuclear_survey |>
  specify(response = arms_reduction, success = "favor") |>
  calculate(stat = "prop")

sample_prop

```

Answer Question 12 in the packet. Then fill in the code below to calculate the bootstrap sampling distribution.

```{code-blanks}
#| blank:
#|   target: arms_reduction
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: favor
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: prop
#|   prefill: true
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token

nuclear_dist <- nuclear_survey |>
  specify(response = arms_reduction, success = "favor") |>
  generate(reps = 5000, type = "bootstrap") |>
  calculate(stat = "prop")

visualize(nuclear_dist)

```

Answer Question 13 in your packet. Then fill in the code below to calculate a 95% confidence interval.

```{code-blanks}
#| blank:
#|   target: 0.95
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token

nuclear_dist |>
  get_confidence_interval(level = 0.95)

```

Use this to answer Questions 14-15, and then **check in** with an instructor.

## Confidence Intervals for Means and Medians

To look at confidence intervals for means and medians, you'll return to the Palmer Archipelago penguins!

Run the code below to see a random 10 rows of the dataset.
```{code-blanks}
slice_sample(palmerpenguins, n = 10)
```

Answer Questions 16-17 in your packet, then fill in the code below to calculate the sample mean body mass.

```{code-blanks}
#| blank:
#|   target: body_mass_g
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: "mean"
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token

sample_mean <- palmerpenguins |>
  specify(response = body_mass_g) |>
  calculate(stat = "mean")

sample_mean

```

Use this to answer Question 18.

Now generate the bootstrap distribution for the mean:

```{code-blanks}
#| blank:
#|   target: body_mass_g
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: "mean"
#|   prefill: true
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: bootstrap
#|   prefill: true
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token

penguin_mean_dist <- palmerpenguins |>
  specify(response = body_mass_g) |>
  generate(reps = 5000, type = "bootstrap") |>
  calculate(stat = "mean")

visualize(penguin_mean_dist)

```

Use that distribution to answer Question 19. Then calculate a 90% confidence interval using the code below.

```{code-blanks}
#| blank:
#|   target: 0.90
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token

penguin_mean_dist |>
  get_confidence_interval(level = 0.90)

```

Answer Question 20 and **check in** with an instructor.

You'll repeat the same process, but you'll estimate the median body mass instead of the mean this time. Answer Questions 21-23 as you complete the code below.

```{code-blanks}
#| blank:
#|   target: body_mass_g
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: median
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token

sample_median <- palmerpenguins |>
  specify(response = body_mass_g) |>
  calculate(stat = "median")

sample_median

```

```{code-blanks}
#| blank:
#|   target: body_mass_g
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: "median"
#|   prefill: true
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token
#| blank:
#|   target: bootstrap
#|   prefill: true
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token

penguin_median_dist <- palmerpenguins |>
  specify(response = body_mass_g) |>
  generate(reps = 5000, type = "bootstrap") |>
  calculate(stat = "median")

visualize(penguin_median_dist)

```

```{code-blanks}
#| blank:
#|   target: 0.90
#|   prefill: false
#|   occurrence: 1
#|   match: token

penguin_median_dist |>
  get_confidence_interval(level = 0.90)

```
